sanskrit: śūdraḥ karoti śuśrūṣāṃ vaiśyā vipaṇijīvinaḥ vayaṃ vadhena jīvāmaḥ kapālaṃ brāhmaṇair vṛtam
english: The Śūdra lives by service, the Vaiśyas by trade and commerce; we warriors live by slaying. The skull-bowl is what the Brahmins seek — each order follows its own mode of life.

sanskrit: kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyaṃ hanti matsyo matsyena jīvati śvā śvānaṃ hanti dāśārha paśya dharmo yathāgataḥ
english: A Kṣatriya slays a Kṣatriya, a fish lives by devouring other fish, a dog kills a dog — O Dāśārha, behold how dharma has come about in this world.

sanskrit: yuddhe kṛṣṇa kalir nityaṃ prāṇāḥ sīdanti saṃyuge balaṃ tu nītimātrāya haṭhe jayaparājayau
english: In battle, O Kṛṣṇa, strife is ever-present and lives perish in the clash; strength serves only to guide strategy, while in obstinate combat both victory and defeat arise.

sanskrit: nātmacchandena bhūtānāṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā nāpy akāle sukhaṃ prāpyaṃ duḥkhaṃ vāpi yadūttama
english: Neither life nor death of living beings comes about by their own will alone; nor can pleasure or pain be obtained outside their proper time, O best of the Yadus.

sanskrit: eko hy api bahūn hanti ghnanty ekaṃ bahavo 'py uta śūraṃ kāpuruṣo hanti ayaśasvī yaśasvinam
english: One man alone may slay many, and many may together slay one; a coward may kill a hero, and a man of no glory may kill one who is glorious.

sanskrit: jayaś caivobhayor dṛṣṭa ubhayoś ca parājayaḥ tathaivāpacayo dṛṣṭo vyapayāne kṣayavyayau
english: Victory and defeat are seen for both sides; likewise decline is seen for both — in retreat come diminution and loss.

sanskrit: sarvathā vṛjinaṃ yuddhaṃ ko ghnan na pratihanyate hatasya ca hṛṣīkeśa samau jayaparājayau
english: War is sinful in every way — who strikes without being struck in return? And for one who is slain, O Hrishikesha, victory and defeat are equal.

sanskrit: parājayaś ca maraṇān manye naiva viśiṣyate yasya syād vijayaḥ kṛṣṇa tasyāpy apacayo dhruvam
english: I consider defeat to be no better than death. And even for one who gains victory, O Kṛṣṇa, decline is certain in the end.

sanskrit: antato dayitaṃ ghnanti ke cid apy apare janāḥ tasyāṅga balahīnasya putrān bhrātṝn apaśyataḥ nirvedo jīvite kṛṣṇa sarvataś copajāyate
english: In the end some people kill even those who are beloved; when that weakened man sees his sons and brothers no more, O Kṛṣṇa, disgust with life arises on every side.

sanskrit: ye hy eva vīrā hrīmanta āryāḥ karuṇavedinaḥ ta eva yuddhe hanyante yavīyān mucyate janaḥ
english: Those heroes who are modest, noble, and sensitive to compassion are precisely the ones who fall in battle; it is the lesser men who survive.

sanskrit: hatvāpy anuśayo nityaṃ parān api janārdana anubandhaś ca pāpo 'tra śeṣaś cāpy avaśiṣyate
english: Even after slaying enemies, O Janārdana, there is ever remorse; and in this, sinful consequence follows after, and a remnant always remains.

sanskrit: śeṣo hi balam āsādya na śeṣam avaśeṣayet sarvocchede ca yatate vairasyāntavidhitsayā
english: For that remnant, gaining strength, would not leave a remnant of its own; it strives for total annihilation, wishing to put an end to the enmity.

sanskrit: jayo vairaṃ prasṛjati duḥkham āste parājitaḥ sukhaṃ praśāntaḥ svapiti hitvā jayaparājayau
english: Victory begets enmity; the defeated one abides in sorrow; one who has laid aside both victory and defeat sleeps in peace and happiness.

sanskrit: jātavairaś ca puruṣo duḥkhaṃ svapiti nityadā anirvṛtena manasā sasarpa iva veśmani
english: A man who has given birth to enmity sleeps in misery every day, his mind without contentment, like a man in a house where a serpent dwells.

sanskrit: utsādayati yaḥ sarvaṃ yaśasā sa viyujyate akīrtiṃ sarvabhūteṣu śāśvatīṃ sa niyacchati
english: One who uproots everything is bereft of fame; he acquires eternal infamy among all living beings.

sanskrit: na hi vairāṇi śāmyanti dīrghakālakṛtāny api ākhyātāraś ca vidyante pumāṃś cotpadyate kule
english: Enmities do not cease, even those created over a long time; there are those who recount them, and men are born again in the clan to avenge them.

sanskrit: na cāpi vairaṃ vaireṇa keśava vyupaśāmyati haviṣāgnir yathā kṛṣṇa bhūya evābhivardhate
english: Nor is enmity ever quelled by enmity, O Keśava; just as fire fed with oblations, O Kṛṣṇa, only grows ever greater.

sanskrit: ato 'nyathā nāsti śāntir nityam antaram antataḥ antaraṃ lipsamānānām ayaṃ doṣo nirantaraḥ
english: There is no peace other than through a different way; those who always seek an opening for attack — this fault is unceasing for them.

sanskrit: pauruṣeyo hi balavān ādhir hṛdayabādhanaḥ tasya tyāgena vā śāntir nivṛttyā manaso 'pi vā
english: The affliction born of manly striving is powerful and torments the heart; peace from it comes either through renunciation or through the withdrawal of the mind.

sanskrit: atha vā mūlaghātena dviṣatāṃ madhusūdana phalanirvṛttir iddhā syāt tan nṛśaṃsataraṃ bhavet
english: Or by striking at the very root of enemies, O Madhusūdana, a blazing cessation of fruit might come about — but that would be even more cruel.

sanskrit: yā tu tyāgena śāntiḥ syāt tad ṛte vadha eva saḥ saṃśayāc ca samucchedād dviṣatām ātmanas tathā
english: The peace that comes through renunciation — without that, it is slaughter itself; and likewise there is the complete annihilation of enemies, and of oneself, from uncertainty.

sanskrit: na ca tyaktuṃ tad icchāmo na cecchāmaḥ kulakṣayam atra yā praṇipātena śāntiḥ saiva garīyasī
english: We do not wish to abandon that, nor do we wish the destruction of the clan. In this situation, the peace that comes through humble submission is indeed the most worthy course.

sanskrit: sarvathā yatamānānām ayuddham abhikāṅkṣatām sāntve pratihate yuddhaṃ prasiddham aparākramam
english: For those who strive in every way and desire non-war, when conciliation is repulsed, war becomes well-established — the result of lack of valor for one side.

sanskrit: pratighātena sāntvasya dāruṇaṃ saṃpravartate tac chunām iva gopāde paṇḍitair upalakṣitam
english: Through the rejection of conciliation something terrible is set in motion; wise men have observed this — it is like the behavior of dogs over a footprint.

sanskrit: lāṅgūlacālanaṃ kṣveḍaḥ pratirāvo vivartanam dantadarśanam ārāvas tato yuddhaṃ pravartate
english: Tail-wagging, snarling, growling back and forth, turning around, baring of teeth, and howling — from these comes the start of a fight.

sanskrit: tatra yo balavān kṛṣṇa jitvā so 'tti tad āmiṣam evam eva manuṣyeṣu viśeṣo nāsti kaś cana
english: There the stronger one, O Kṛṣṇa, having conquered, devours that prey. Even so among men there is no distinction whatsoever — it is the same.

sanskrit: sarvathā tv etad ucitaṃ durbaleṣu balīyasām anādaro virodhaś ca praṇipātī hi durbalaḥ
english: In every way this is fitting behavior of the strong toward the weak — disregard and opposition; for the weak man indeed submits in supplication.

sanskrit: pitā rājā ca vṛddhaś ca sarvathā mānam arhati tasmān mānyaś ca pūjyaś ca dhṛtarāṣṭro janārdana
english: A father, a king, and an elder deserve honor in every way; therefore Dhṛtarāṣṭra is worthy of honor and worship, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: putrasnehas tu balavān dhṛtarāṣṭrasya mādhava sa putravaśam āpannaḥ praṇipātaṃ prahāsyati
english: But the love for his son is powerful in Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Mādhava; fallen under the sway of his son, he will abandon any submission to us.

sanskrit: tatra kiṃ manyase kṛṣṇa prāptakālam anantaram katham arthāc ca dharmāc ca na hīyemahi mādhava
english: In that situation, what do you think, O Kṛṣṇa, is the course befitting the moment? How may we not fall short in both material purpose and righteousness, O Mādhava?

sanskrit: īdṛśe hy arthakṛcchre 'smin kam anyaṃ madhusūdana upasaṃpraṣṭum arhāmi tvām ṛte puruṣottama
english: In this difficulty of purpose, O Madhusūdana, whom else could I fittingly consult apart from you, O best of men?

sanskrit: priyaś ca priyakāmaś ca gatijñaḥ sarvakarmaṇām ko hi kṛṣṇāsti nas tvādṛk sarvaniścayavit suhṛt
english: You are dear to us and you desire our welfare; you know the right course in all matters — who is there for us like you, O Kṛṣṇa, a friend who knows every resolution?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca dharmarājaṃ janārdanaḥ ubhayor eva vām arthe yāsyāmi kurusaṃsadam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Janārdana replied to the king of dharma: 'For the benefit of you both, I will go to the assembly of the Kurus.'

sanskrit: śamaṃ tatra labheyaṃ ced yuṣmadartham ahāpayan puṇyaṃ me sumahad rājaṃś caritaṃ syān mahāphalam
english: 'If I achieve peace there without sacrificing your interests, O king, that would be a very great meritorious act for me, bearing a great reward.'

sanskrit: mocayeyaṃ mṛtyupāśāt saṃrabdhān kurusṛñjayān pāṇḍavān dhārtarāṣṭrāṃś ca sarvāṃ ca pṛthivīm imām
english: 'I would free from the noose of death the enraged Kurus and Sṛñjayas, the Pāṇḍavas, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and this entire earth.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na mamaitan mataṃ kṛṣṇa yat tvaṃ yāyāḥ kurūn prati suyodhanaḥ sūktam api na kariṣyati te vacaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: It is not my view, O Kṛṣṇa, that you should go to the Kurus — Suyodhana will not act upon your words even if they are well-spoken.

sanskrit: sametaṃ pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ suyodhanavaśānugam teṣāṃ madhyāvataraṇaṃ tava kṛṣṇa na rocaye
english: The assembled royal Kṣatriyas who follow Suyodhana's will — I do not welcome your entering into their midst, O Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: na hi naḥ prīṇayed dravyaṃ na devatvaṃ kutaḥ sukham na ca sarvāmaraiśvaryaṃ tava rodhena mādhava
english: Neither wealth nor divine status — still less happiness — nor even the sovereignty of all the gods would please us if it came at the cost of obstructing you, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca jānāmy etāṃ mahārāja dhārtarāṣṭrasya pāpatām avācyās tu bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvaloke mahīkṣitām
english: The Blessed Lord said: I know, O great king, the wickedness of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son; yet we shall become beyond reproach in the eyes of all kings in every world.

sanskrit: na cāpi mama paryāptāḥ sahitāḥ sarvapārthivāḥ kruddhasya pramukhe sthātuṃ siṃhasyevetare mṛgāḥ
english: Nor indeed are all the kings assembled together sufficient to stand before me when I am angered — just as lesser creatures cannot stand before a lion.

sanskrit: atha cet te pravarteran mayi kiṃ cid asāṃpratam nirdaheyaṃ kurūn sarvān iti me dhīyate matiḥ
english: And if they were to act against me in any improper way, I would burn all the Kurus to ashes — so my mind resolves.

sanskrit: na jātu gamanaṃ tatra bhavet pārtha nirarthakam arthaprāptiḥ kadā cit syād antato vāpy avācyatā
english: The journey there will certainly not be fruitless, O Pārtha; either the attainment of the purpose will come at some point, or at the very least there will be freedom from reproach.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yat tubhyaṃ rocate kṛṣṇa svasti prāpnuhi kauravān kṛtārthaṃ svastimantaṃ tvāṃ drakṣyāmi punarāgatam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whatever pleases you, O Kṛṣṇa — go well to the Kauravas; I shall see you return with your purpose accomplished and in good health.

sanskrit: viṣvaksena kurūn gatvā bhāratāñ śamayeḥ prabho yathā sarve sumanasaḥ saha syāmaḥ sucetasaḥ
english: O Viṣvaksena, O lord, going to the Kurus, may you pacify the Bharatas so that we may all be together with glad minds and serene hearts.

sanskrit: bhrātā cāsi sakhā cāsi bībhatsor mama ca priyaḥ sauhṛdenāviśaṅkyo 'si svasti prāpnuhi bhūtaye
english: You are a brother, you are a friend, and you are dear to Bībhatsu and to me; by reason of our friendship you are beyond suspicion — go well for the good of all.

sanskrit: asmān vettha parān vettha vetthārthaṃ vettha bhāṣitam yad yad asmaddhitaṃ kṛṣṇa tat tad vācyaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: You know us, you know the others, you know the purpose, you know the proper words — whatever is for our benefit, O Kṛṣṇa, that is what you should say to Suyodhana.

sanskrit: yad yad dharmeṇa saṃyuktam upapadyed dhitaṃ vacaḥ tat tat keśava bhāṣethāḥ sāntvaṃ vā yadi vetarat
english: Whatever words joined with righteousness and beneficial counsel may be appropriate, those speak, O Keśava — whether conciliatory or otherwise.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca saṃjayasya śrutaṃ vākyaṃ bhavataś ca śrutaṃ mayā sarvaṃ jānāmy abhiprāyaṃ teṣāṃ ca bhavataś ca yaḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: I have heard Sañjaya's words and I have heard yours; I know in full the intentions both of them and of you.

sanskrit: tava dharmāśritā buddhis teṣāṃ vairāśritā matiḥ yad ayuddhena labhyeta tat te bahumataṃ bhavet
english: Your understanding is grounded in dharma; their mind is grounded in enmity. What can be gained without war — that would be greatly esteemed by you.

sanskrit: na ca tan naiṣṭhikaṃ karma kṣatriyasya viśāṃ pate āhur āśramiṇaḥ sarve yad bhaikṣaṃ kṣatriyaś caret
english: But that is not the final duty of a Kṣatriya, O lord of peoples; all those who live in the stages of life say that a Kṣatriya should not live by begging.

sanskrit: jayo vadho vā saṃgrāme dhātrā diṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ svadharmaḥ kṣatriyasyaiṣa kārpaṇyaṃ na praśasyate
english: Victory or death in battle — this is eternally ordained by the Creator; this is the own-duty of a Kṣatriya. Weakness of spirit is not commended.

sanskrit: na hi kārpaṇyam āsthāya śakyā vṛttir yudhiṣṭhira vikramasva mahābāho jahi śatrūn ariṃdama
english: Resorting to faint-heartedness, livelihood cannot be sustained, O Yudhiṣṭhira. Show valor, O mighty-armed one; slay the enemies, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: atigṛddhāḥ kṛtasnehā dīrghakālaṃ sahoṣitāḥ kṛtamitrāḥ kṛtabalā dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ paraṃtapa
english: The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are excessively greedy, they have cultivated alliances, they have dwelt together for a long time, they have made friends and built up strength, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: na paryāyo 'sti yat sāmyaṃ tvayi kuryur viśāṃ pate balavattāṃ hi manyante bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādibhiḥ
english: There is no means by which they would treat you as an equal, O lord of peoples; for they consider themselves powerful on account of Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and others.

sanskrit: yāvac ca mārdavenaitān rājann upacariṣyasi tāvad ete hariṣyanti tava rājyam ariṃdama
english: And for as long as you attend to them with gentleness, O king, for that long will they take away your kingdom, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: nānukrośān na kārpaṇyān na ca dharmārthakāraṇāt alaṃ kartuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrās tava kāmam ariṃdama
english: Neither out of compassion, nor out of weakness, nor for the sake of dharma or material interest are the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra capable of fulfilling your desire, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: etad eva nimittaṃ te pāṇḍavās tu yathā tvayi nānvatapyanta kaupīnaṃ tāvat kṛtvāpi duṣkaram
english: This very reason — that the Pāṇḍavas did not repent even of wearing a loincloth for your sake, difficult as that was — this is the cause that now stands before you.

sanskrit: pitāmahasya droṇasya vidurasya ca dhīmataḥ paśyatāṃ kurumukhyānāṃ sarveṣām eva tattvataḥ
english: Before the grandfather Bhīṣma, before Droṇa, before the wise Vidura, before the assembled chiefs of the Kurus who saw everything as it truly was —

sanskrit: dānaśīlaṃ mṛduṃ dāntaṃ dharmakāmam anuvratam yat tvām upadhinā rājan dyūtenāvañcayat tadā na cāpatrapate pāpo nṛśaṃsas tena karmaṇā
english: — he who is given to charity, gentle, self-controlled, devoted to dharma, and faithful — that you, O king, he deceived by fraud through gambling; and that wicked, cruel man feels no shame on account of that act.

sanskrit: tathāśīlasamācāre rājan mā praṇayaṃ kṛthāḥ vadhyās te sarvalokasya kiṃ punas tava bhārata
english: With one of such character and conduct, O king, do not show affection; he deserves to be slain by all the world — how much more so by you, O Bharata.

sanskrit: vāgbhis tv apratirūpābhir atudat sakanīyasam ślāghamānaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ san bhāṣate bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: With words utterly unfitting, he taunted one who did not deserve it; he boasts and speaks joyfully among his brothers.

sanskrit: etāvat pāṇḍavānāṃ hi nāsti kiṃ cid iha svakam nāmadheyaṃ ca gotraṃ ca tad apy eṣāṃ na śiṣyate
english: 'The Pāṇḍavas have nothing at all of their own here — not even their name and lineage will remain to them.'

sanskrit: kālena mahatā caiṣāṃ bhaviṣyati parābhavaḥ prakṛtiṃ te bhajiṣyanti naṣṭaprakṛtayo janāḥ
english: 'After a great length of time their ruin will come; those people who have lost their following will return to their natural state.'

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca paruṣā vācaḥ sa samudīrayan ślāghate jñātimadhye sma tvayi pravrajite vanam
english: Uttering these and other harsh words, he boasts among his kinsmen now that you have gone out to the forest.

sanskrit: ye tatrāsan samānītās te dṛṣṭvā tvām anāgasam aśrukaṇṭhā rudantaś ca sabhāyām āsate tadā
english: Those who were gathered there, seeing you blameless yet wronged, sat in the assembly hall at that time with tears in their throats, weeping.

sanskrit: na cainam abhyanandaṃs te rājāno brāhmaṇaiḥ saha sarve duryodhanaṃ tatra nindanti sma sabhāsadaḥ
english: Those kings did not applaud him; together with the Brahmins, all the members of that assembly condemned Duryodhana there.

sanskrit: kulīnasya ca yā nindā vadhaś cāmitrakarśana mahāguṇo vadho rājan na tu nindā kujīvikā
english: The censure of a man of noble birth, and slaying — O crusher of enemies, slaying is a greater virtue, O king; but censure is a base way of living.

sanskrit: tadaiva nihato rājan yadaiva nirapatrapaḥ ninditaś ca mahārāja pṛthivyāṃ sarvarājasu
english: He was slain at that very moment, O king, the moment he became shameless and was condemned, O great king, among all the kings of the earth.

sanskrit: īṣatkāryo vadhas tasya yasya cāritram īdṛśam praskambhanapratistabdhaś chinnamūla iva drumaḥ
english: The slaying of one whose character is like this requires little effort; propped up and stiffened artificially, he is like a tree whose roots have been cut.

sanskrit: vadhyaḥ sarpa ivānāryaḥ sarvalokasya durmatiḥ jahy enaṃ tvam amitraghna mā rājan vicikitsithāḥ
english: That ignoble, evil-minded man deserves to be slain by all the world, like a serpent. Slay him, O destroyer of enemies — do not hesitate, O king.

sanskrit: sarvathā tvatkṣamaṃ caitad rocate ca mamānagha yat tvaṃ pitari bhīṣme ca praṇipātaṃ samācareḥ
english: In every way this is fitting for you, and it pleases me also, O sinless one — that you should offer humble submission to your father and to Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu sarvalokasya gatvā chetsyāmi saṃśayam yeṣām asti dvidhābhāvo rājan duryodhanaṃ prati
english: But I, going there, will cut away the doubt of all those in the world who are of two minds regarding Duryodhana, O king.

sanskrit: madhye rājñām ahaṃ tatra prātipauruṣikān guṇān tava saṃkīrtayiṣyāmi ye ca tasya vyatikramāḥ
english: In the midst of the kings assembled there, I will proclaim your virtues befitting a true man, and also his transgressions.

sanskrit: bruvatas tatra me vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam niśamya pārthivāḥ sarve nānājanapadeśvarāḥ
english: Having heard my words spoken there — words joined with righteousness and purpose, and truly beneficial — all the kings and rulers of various countries —

sanskrit: tvayi saṃpratipatsyante dharmātmā satyavāg iti tasmiṃś cādhigamiṣyanti yathā lobhād avartata
english: — will recognize in you a soul of dharma and a speaker of truth; and in him they will discover how he acted out of greed.

sanskrit: garhayiṣyāmi caivainaṃ paurajānapadeṣv api vṛddhabālān upādāya cāturvarṇyasamāgame
english: And I will reproach him even among the townspeople and country folk, taking in the old and the young alike, in the assembly of the four orders of society.

sanskrit: śamaṃ ced yācamānas tvaṃ na dharmaṃ tatra lapsyase kurūn vigarhayiṣyanti dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca pārthivāḥ
english: If, while you are seeking peace there, dharma is not obtained, the kings will censure the Kurus and Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tasmiṃl lokaparityakte kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣyate hate duryodhane rājan yad anyat kriyatām iti
english: When he who is abandoned by the world is slain — when Duryodhana is slain — O king, what other task will remain to be done?

sanskrit: yātvā cāhaṃ kurūn sarvān yuṣmadartham ahāpayan yatiṣye praśamaṃ kartuṃ lakṣayiṣye ca ceṣṭitam
english: And going to all the Kurus, without sacrificing your interests, I will strive to bring about peace and I will observe their conduct closely.

sanskrit: kauravāṇāṃ pravṛttiṃ ca gatvā yuddhādhikārikām niśāmya vinivartiṣye jayāya tava bhārata
english: And going there, having observed the Kauravas' course of action — one bent on war — I will return for the sake of your victory, O Bharata.
